name: Anagó / Lucumí
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Concordia, Maria J. 2012. The Anagó Language of Cuba. M.A. thesis, Florida International University (FIU Electronic Theses and Dissertations 732). Secondary: Uguru, Joy O. 2021. A Lexico-phonetic Comparison of Olukumi and Lukumi. Lexikos 31:214-233, sec. 3.2.
catalog_locator: Concordia 2012, ch. on structure, pp. 65-66 (pp. 73-74), examples (1)-(2); Uguru 2021 p. 222-223 sec. 3.2.1-3.2.2
catalog_quote: Anagó does not follow this pattern. The vowels in Anagó do not have tones; the more correct description for the pattern is stress. The Anagó stress pattern is shown in example two. The stress is not accompanied by a raising or lowering of the pitch, as in Yoruba. See example two. (2) Omí /o mi/ (water) orí /o ri/ (head) óke /o kə/ (mountain) iché. /e čə/ (work) The Anagó language does not have tonal vowels but rather follows a Spanish stress pattern with the stress usually falling on the last syllable of the word. The stress pattern of Anagó is a subject that requires further study which is not within the scope of this thesis. The examination of Anagó stress patterns and their relationship to the Yoruba tonal system should be an area of further research ...

audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: the deciding passage is verbatim at Concordia 2012 pp. 65-66 and the secondary Uguru 2021 sec. 3.2 pp. 222-223 is verbatim too; Castellanos & Castellanos 1992 p. 296 (held) and Uguru & Okeke 2020 p. 537 (downloaded now) independently agree that Yoruba tone is gone and a Spanish-type accent replaced it, and none contradicts final stress. The record is 'thin' rather than well-sourced because the deciding source is a non-linguistics M.A. thesis whose author explicitly defers the stress analysis, hedges with 'usually', and includes a non-final example (óke); there is no grammar, phonology or instrumental study of this liturgical register in Glottolog (0 descriptive refs) or Crossref, so 'fixed-unreviewed, final, non-strict' is a fair reading of what exists.
